text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least four members of a radical Shi'ite Moslem group were shot dead in a brawl with police during prayers to mark the end of Ramadan fast in the northern city of Kano on Friday.
- Many senior management staff of Ajaokuta steel project in central Nigeria may have been retired, official sources said.
- Moslems offer prayers nationwide for peace in Nigeria as they mark end of Ramadan fast.
- Nigeria's under-17 football team beat Portugal 2-0 to qualify for final of African and European Meridien championship in Lisbon.
- National carrier Nigeria Airways sends plane to Tel Aviv to bring home Christian pilgrims stranded in Israel.

- The five registered political parties start informal consultations among themselves on how to seek financial assistance from the federal government for the impending registration of voters and local council elections.
- Pump stations in Lagos ration fuel as supplies from depots trickle into the metropolis.
- Electoral commission and the transition to civil rule implementation committee mobilise for registration of voters which commences nationwide on Monday.

- On occasion of Moslem festival of Eid al-Fitr, the Sultan of Sokoto, spiritual leader of Nigerian Moslems, condemns street begging while Emir of Ilorin in central Nigeria bans women from wearing mini skirts in his domain.
- Vision 2010 committee planning Nigeria's future to hold the next in its series of workshops on development in the capital Abuja from Tuesday to Thursday.
- Thousands of youths in the oil-producing Rivers state stage a rally in the state capital Port Harcourt in support of military ruler General Sani Abacha.
